description: Florentine Dominican nun (1522-1590) who spent twelve years in weekly ecstatic meditation on the Passion. She was also a skilled administrator, trusted advisor and friend to saints.

name: Saint Claude de la Colombière
description: French Jesuit (1641-1682) who became the spiritual director of Saint Margaret Mary Alacoque and promoted devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, trusting his own life to divine providence.
patronOf: Spiritual directors, those devoted to the Sacred Heart

name: Saint Juliana of Nicomedia
description: Young woman martyred around 304 after refusing to marry a pagan official or to give up her faith. Tradition says she endured prison and torture with serene patience.
patronOf: Those facing pressure to abandon their faith

name: The Seven Holy Founders of the Servite Order
description: Seven Florentine merchants who withdrew to Monte Senario in 1233 to live in prayer and devotion to Our Lady of Sorrows. They founded the Servants of Mary.

name: Saint Conrad of Piacenza
description: Italian nobleman (1290-1351) who accidentally set a fire while hunting, accepted blame and gave away his wealth. He lived as a hermit in Sicily, famed for prayer and healing.
patronOf: Hermits, those with hernias, the repentant

name: Saints Jacinta and Francisco Marto
description: Two Portuguese shepherd children who saw Our Lady at Fatima in 1917. They died young, in 1919 and 1920, after offering their sufferings for sinners, and were canonized in 2017.
patronOf: Children, those who pray for sinners

name: Saint Peter Damian
description: Italian monk and cardinal (1007-1072) who worked to reform the clergy and encouraged a life of simple, penitential prayer. He was named a Doctor of the Church for his writings.
patronOf: Reformers, monks, those who seek humility

name: The Chair of Saint Peter
description: A feast celebrating the ministry of Peter as shepherd of the Church. The empty 'chair' stands for the teaching authority entrusted to Peter and his successors.
patronOf: The Pope, the unity of the Church

name: The Finding of the Head of Saint John the Baptist
description: A feast recalling the discovery of the relic of the head of John the Baptist, the forerunner who prepared the way for Christ with the call to repentance.

name: Saint Walburga
description: English abbess (c. 710-779) who went with her brothers to Germany to help Saint Boniface and led the double monastery of Heidenheim. She is invoked for healing.

name: Saint Porphyry of Gaza
description: Bishop of Gaza (c. 347-420) who stayed firm in a city where most people remained pagan. He worked patiently for conversions and cared for the poor of his diocese.

name: Pope Saint Hilarius
description: Pope from 461 to 468 who defended the unity of the Church, upheld the teaching of Chalcedon and cared for the poor of Rome during troubled years.

name: Saint Oswald of Worcester
description: Archbishop of York (d. 992) who helped renew monastic life in England, founded the abbey of Ramsey and was loved for humility and care for the poor.

name: Saint David of Wales
description: Sixth-century bishop and abbot who founded monasteries across Wales and lived a life of simplicity and prayer. His last words, 'Be joyful, keep the faith', are still quoted in Wales.

name: Saint Chad of Lichfield
description: Seventh-century English bishop who walked the countryside to preach, a student of Saint Aidan. As bishop of Lichfield he served humbly and was loved by his flock.
patronOf: Missionaries, those who walk long roads

name: Saint Casimir of Poland
description: Polish prince (1458-1484) who gave his wealth to the poor, preferred prayer to power, and chose chastity and a simple life. He died of illness at 25 and is a patron of Poland and Lithuania.

name: Saint Piran of Cornwall
description: Irish-born abbot (d. c. 480) who settled in Cornwall and taught the people to farm and to love Christ. Tradition says he rediscovered tin smelting. He is honoured as patron of Cornwall.

name: Saint Colette
description: French Poor Clare nun (1381-1447) who reformed her order, restoring the strict poverty of Saint Clare and founding many convents across Europe.
patronOf: Reformers, those who seek renewal in the Church

name: Saint Frances of Rome
description: Roman noblewoman (1384-1440) who cared for the poor and the sick during plague and war, and founded a community of oblates. She is said to have had a guardian angel always visible to her.

name: Saint John Ogilvie
description: Scottish Jesuit (1579-1615) who returned to a hostile Scotland to minister secretly to Catholics. He was arrested and hanged in Glasgow, and is Scotland's only canonized post-Reformation saint.
patronOf: Scotland, those who suffer for conscience

name: Saint Eulogius of Cordoba
description: Priest and writer in Moorish Spain who encouraged Christians facing persecution. He was beheaded in 859 for sheltering a young woman who had converted to Christianity.

name: Saint Maximilian of Tebessa
description: A young North African who refused military service in 295 because of his faith. The Roman proconsul sentenced him to death and he went to his execution with joy.

name: Saint Euphrasia
description: Fifth-century virgin who lived in a convent in Egypt and led a life of obedient service and fasting. She was esteemed for humility and gentleness.

name: Saint Matilda of Ringelheim
description: Queen of Germany (c. 895-968), mother of Emperor Otto the Great. Widowed, she devoted herself to charity and prayer, founded monasteries, and cared for the poor.

name: Saint Louise de Marillac
description: French widow (1591-1660) who co-founded the Daughters of Charity with Saint Vincent de Paul, teaching her sisters to see Christ in the poor and the sick.

name: Saint Heribert of Cologne
description: Archbishop of Cologne (c. 970-1021) who was chancellor to Emperor Otto III. He was known for justice, generosity to the poor, and for ending a drought through prayer.

name: Saint Cuthbert of Lindisfarne
description: Northumbrian monk and bishop (c. 634-687) who walked the hills teaching the poor and later lived as a hermit on Farne Island. His body was carried by monks through northern England.

name: Saint Nicholas Owen
description: English Jesuit lay brother (d. 1606) who built hiding places for priests during the persecution of Catholics. Arrested and tortured to death, he never revealed those he protected.

name: Saint Turibius of Mogrovejo
description: Spanish lawyer who became archbishop of Lima (1538-1606). He crossed his enormous diocese on foot, learned native languages, and defended the Indigenous people from abuse.
patronOf: Latin American bishops, those who serve the poor

name: Saint Oscar Romero
description: Archbishop of San Salvador (1917-1980) who spoke for the poor and condemned violence during El Salvador's civil war. He was shot while celebrating Mass and canonized in 2018.
patronOf: El Salvador, defenders of justice, the poor

name: The Annunciation of the Lord
description: The angel Gabriel tells Mary that she will bear the Son of God, and she answers 'let it be done to me according to your word'. The feast falls nine months before Christmas.
patronOf: Mothers, those who say yes to God

name: Saint Ludger
description: Frisian bishop (c. 742-809) who preached in Saxony, founded the monastery of Werden and became the first bishop of Munster. Charlemagne trusted him with the mission to the Saxons.

name: Saint Rupert of Salzburg
description: Bishop and missionary (c. 660-718) in Bavaria who founded the church of Salzburg and the monastery of Saint Peter. He is honoured as apostle of Bavaria and Austria.

name: Pope Saint Sixtus III
description: Pope from 432 to 440 who built the basilica of Saint Mary Major in Rome after the Council of Ephesus affirmed Mary as Mother of God. He worked for peace between the churches of East and West.

name: Saint Berthold of Calabria
description: Crusader and hermit who settled on Mount Carmel in the twelfth century with a small group of companions. He is traditionally counted as the first superior of the Carmelite order.

name: Saint Benjamin the Deacon
description: Persian deacon martyred in 424 after refusing to stop preaching the Gospel when released from prison. His fearless witness and gentleness are recalled in the Eastern and Western Churches.
patronOf: Deacons, those who speak the truth in danger

name: Saint Francis of Paola
description: Italian hermit (1416-1507) who founded the Minim friars, devoted to humility, penance and charity. He advised kings and the poor alike and is a patron of seafarers.

name: Saint Richard of Chichester
description: English bishop (1197-1253) who served his flock faithfully despite royal opposition. He gave generously to the poor and is remembered for the prayer 'to know Thee more clearly, love Thee more dearly'.
patronOf: Bishops, coachmen, those who seek to know Christ

name: Saint Isidore of Seville
description: Spanish bishop (c. 560-636) and scholar who wrote an encyclopedia of knowledge, preserving ancient learning for the Middle Ages. He is named a Doctor of the Church.

name: Saint Vincent Ferrer
description: Spanish Dominican (1350-1419) who preached across Europe, calling many to conversion. He helped to end the Western Schism and worked tirelessly for peace.

name: Blessed Michael Rua
description: First successor of Saint John Bosco (1837-1910) as head of the Salesians. He extended the order across continents and kept alive the spirit of joyful service to young people.

name: Saint John Baptist de La Salle
description: French priest (1651-1719) who founded the Brothers of the Christian Schools and created methods of teaching that shaped modern education. He gave his fortune to educate poor boys.

name: Saint Julie Billiart
description: French religious (1751-1816) who overcame years of paralysis to found the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur and dedicate her life to educating girls. She is known for joyful trust in God.
patronOf: Those who are ill, teachers, the disabled

name: Saint Fulbert of Chartres
description: Bishop of Chartres (c. 960-1028) who rebuilt his cathedral after a fire and made its school a centre of learning. He wrote letters and hymns and promoted devotion to Mary.

name: Saint Stanislaus of Krakow
description: Bishop of Krakow (1030-1079) who rebuked the king for his injustice and was killed while celebrating Mass. He is Poland's patron saint and a witness to the Church's moral voice.
patronOf: Poland, Krakow, those who speak for justice

name: Saint Zeno of Verona
description: Bishop of Verona (d. c. 371) who taught clearly and gently, baptised many converts and protected the poor. His sermons survive and show a kind-hearted pastor.

name: Pope Saint Martin I
description: Pope (d. 655) who condemned an error about Christ's will and was arrested by the emperor, mistreated and exiled to Crimea. He is honoured as the last pope to die as a martyr.
patronOf: Those who suffer for the truth

name: Saint Lidwina of Schiedam
description: Dutch woman (1380-1433) who, after a skating accident, was bedridden for 38 years. She united her sufferings to Christ and became a model of patience and a counsellor to many.

name: Saint Damien of Molokai
description: Belgian priest (1840-1889) who volunteered to live with people with leprosy in Hawaii, building homes and churches. He contracted the disease himself and died serving them.

name: Pope Saint Anicetus
description: Second-century bishop of Rome who met with Saint Polycarp to discuss the date of Easter and remained in friendship despite differences. He held firm against false teaching.

name: Saint Apollonius the Apologist
description: Roman senator martyred in about 185 after publicly defending the Christian faith before the Senate. His reasoned defence made him an early model of Christian intellectual witness.

name: Pope Saint Leo IX
description: German pope (1002-1054) who worked tirelessly to reform the Church, fight corruption and renew the clergy. He travelled widely across Europe as pope.

name: Saint Agnes of Montepulciano
description: Italian Dominican (1268-1317) who entered a convent at 14 and became abbess at 20. She founded a monastery and was known for deep prayer and the gift of healing.

name: Saints Soter and Caius
description: Two second- and third-century popes who led the Church of Rome through persecution. Soter wrote to Corinth with great compassion; Caius served at a time of fierce trials.

name: Saint Fidelis of Sigmaringen
description: German lawyer turned Capuchin friar (1577-1622) who preached to Protestants in Switzerland and was martyred by a mob. He was known for kindness toward the poor.

name: Pope Saint Cletus
description: Early successor of Saint Peter as bishop of Rome, listed in the Roman Canon of the Mass. Little is known about him, but the Church honours him as an apostolic father.

name: Saint Zita of Lucca
description: Italian domestic servant (c. 1212-1272) who worked faithfully for one family all her life, giving to the poor from what she received. Her cheerful service made her beloved.

name: Pope Saint Pius V
description: Dominican pope (1504-1572) who implemented the reforms of the Council of Trent, standardised the Roman Missal and encouraged the Rosary. He lived simply and cared for the poor.

name: Saint Joseph the Worker
description: Pope Pius XII set this feast in 1955 to honour Joseph the carpenter and the dignity of human work. Joseph shows that ordinary labour offered with love becomes a path to holiness.

name: Saints Philip and James the Apostles
description: Two of the twelve apostles. Philip brought Nathanael to Jesus and asked 'show us the Father'; James the Less led the church in Jerusalem. Both were martyred for the faith.
patronOf: Hatters, pastry cooks, the Church in Jerusalem

name: Saint Florian
description: Roman army officer who was martyred in 304 in Austria for refusing to persecute Christians. He is invoked for protection against fire and is the patron of firefighters.
patronOf: Firefighters, those at risk from fire

name: Saint Angelus of Jerusalem
description: Carmelite friar and preacher of the thirteenth century, a convert from Judaism who preached in Sicily. He was killed by a man he had publicly rebuked for sin.

name: Saint John before the Latin Gate
description: Tradition says the apostle John was plunged into boiling oil at the Latin Gate in Rome during Domitian's persecution and emerged unharmed. A church in Rome marks the place.
patronOf: Those in danger, Christians under persecution

name: Saint Rose Venerini
description: Italian teacher (1656-1728) who opened the first public schools for girls in Italy. She trained teachers and founded the Religious Teachers Filippini, known for gentle persistence.

name: Julian of Norwich
description: English anchoress (1342-c. 1416) who wrote the earliest surviving book in English by a woman, 'Revelations of Divine Love'. Her words 'all shall be well' have comforted generations.
patronOf: Mystics, those in doubt or distress

name: Saint Pachomius
description: Egyptian founder of communal monastic life (c. 292-348). He gathered hermits into monasteries governed by a rule, shaping Christian monasticism in both East and West.

name: Saint Ignatius of Laconi
description: Sardinian Capuchin lay brother (1701-1781) who for forty years begged alms for his friary. Children and the poor loved him for his humility and gentle spirit.

name: Saint Pancras of Rome
description: Young Roman martyr who died around 304 at the age of fourteen for refusing to sacrifice to idols. His church in London gave the district its name.

name: Our Lady of Fatima
description: On May 13, 1917, the Virgin Mary appeared to three shepherd children in Fatima, Portugal, asking for prayer, penance and the daily Rosary for peace in the world.

name: Saint Matthias the Apostle
description: Chosen by lot to fill the place of Judas among the twelve, according to the Acts of the Apostles. He had followed Jesus from his baptism and witnessed the resurrection.

name: Saint Brendan the Navigator
description: Irish abbot (c. 484-577) who founded monasteries and, according to tradition, sailed westward with companions on a seven-year voyage in search of the 'Promised Land of the Saints'.

name: Saint Paschal Baylon
description: Spanish Franciscan lay brother (1540-1592) who worked as a porter, shepherd and doorkeeper. He had deep devotion to the Eucharist and is patron of Eucharistic congresses.

name: Pope Saint John I
description: Pope from 523 to 526 who travelled to Constantinople to ask the emperor to stop persecuting Arians. He was imprisoned by the Gothic king Theodoric and died in prison.

name: Saint Celestine V
description: Hermit elected pope in 1294 at age 79. Overwhelmed by the office, he resigned after five months to return to prayer, an act that has intrigued the Church ever since.
patronOf: Hermits, those who step down with humility

name: Saint Bernardine of Siena
description: Italian Franciscan (1380-1444) who preached tirelessly across Italy, urged devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus and cared for plague victims. He called people to reconciliation.

name: Saint Christopher Magallanes and Companions
description: Twenty-five Mexican martyrs, mostly priests, killed between 1915 and 1937 during religious persecution. Many died shouting 'Viva Cristo Rey!' and forgiving their executioners.

name: Saint Ivo of Kermartin
description: Breton judge and priest (1253-1303) known as the 'advocate of the poor'. He gave justice freely to the poor, mediated disputes and lived simply, sharing his food with the hungry.

name: Saint Bede the Venerable
description: English monk of Jarrow (c. 673-735) who wrote the 'Ecclesiastical History of the English People' and many commentaries. He is the only English Doctor of the Church.

name: Saint Bernard of Menthon
description: Alpine archdeacon (c. 1020-1081) who founded hospices on the passes now named for him to shelter pilgrims and travellers. The famous rescue dogs were later named after him.

name: Saint Maximinus of Trier
description: Fourth-century bishop of Trier who sheltered Saint Athanasius when he was exiled. He defended the faith of Nicaea in Gaul and was honoured for hospitality.

name: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
description: Mary, newly pregnant, travels to visit her cousin Elizabeth. Elizabeth greets her as 'blessed among women' and Mary responds with the Magnificat, her great song of praise.
patronOf: Pregnant women, those who serve others

name: Saint Justin Martyr
description: Philosopher turned Christian teacher (c. 100-165) who explained the faith to Roman audiences and defended believers before the emperor. He was beheaded in Rome.

name: Saints Marcellinus and Peter
description: A priest and an exorcist killed in Rome around 304 under Diocletian. They are named in the Roman Canon, and their story is told by their executioner who later converted.

name: Saint Charles Lwanga and Companions
description: Twenty-two young Ugandan men, pages at the royal court, who were martyred in 1886 for refusing to abandon their faith. They are honoured as protomartyrs of Africa's Great Lakes.

name: Saint Francis Caracciolo
description: Italian priest (1563-1608) who co-founded the Minor Clerks Regular and promoted perpetual adoration of the Blessed Sacrament. He served prisoners and the poor.

name: Saint Norbert of Xanten
description: German bishop (c. 1075-1134) who was converted after a near-fatal lightning strike and founded the Premonstratensian canons. He promoted devotion to the Eucharist.

name: Saint Antony Mary Gianelli
description: Italian bishop of Bobbio (1789-1846) and founder of the Sisters of Mary Dell'Orto. He cared for those in need during famine and strengthened the faith of his people.

name: Saint William of York
description: English archbishop (d. 1154) who was twice deposed through church politics and twice returned. He was loved for his gentleness and for caring for the poor of York.

name: Saint Henry of Treviso
description: Italian layman (d. 1315) who worked as a day labourer and lived in poverty. He prayed daily in the cathedral, and after he died the people of Treviso honoured him as a saint.

name: Pope Saint Leo III
description: Pope from 795 to 816 who crowned Charlemagne emperor on Christmas Day in 800. He faced violent opposition in Rome and was known for building churches and defending the faith.

name: Saint Methodius I of Constantinople
description: Patriarch of Constantinople (c. 788-847) who suffered persecution for defending holy images and led the Church to its 'Triumph of Orthodoxy' in 843.

name: Saint Germaine Cousin
description: French shepherdess (1579-1601) with a disabled hand who was mistreated by her family. She fed the poor from her scarce bread and prayed daily at Mass with great faith.

name: Saint John Francis Regis
description: French Jesuit (1597-1640) who preached missions in the mountains of the Cevennes, cared for the poor and the sick and founded shelters for those in need.

name: Saint Albert Chmielowski
description: Polish painter and soldier (1845-1916) who gave up art to serve the destitute of Krakow. He founded the Albertine Brothers and Sisters and was a friend to Saint John Paul II's family.
patronOf: The homeless, artists, those who give up everything

name: Saints Mark and Marcellian
description: Twin brothers martyred in Rome around 286. Tradition says they were tied to pillars and pierced with nails, singing praise as they died, and were buried on the Via Ardeatina.

name: Saint Romuald
description: Italian monk (c. 951-1027) who founded the Camaldolese hermits and spent decades travelling to renew monastic life. He taught a gentle, contemplative approach to the Psalms.

name: Pope Saint Silverius
description: Pope from 536 to 537 who was deposed through political intrigue and exiled to a small island, where he died of hardship. He is honoured as a martyr for the faith.

name: Saint Aloysius Gonzaga
description: Italian Jesuit (1568-1591) who renounced a princely inheritance to enter the Society of Jesus. He died at 23 while caring for victims of plague in Rome.

name: Saint Joseph Cafasso
description: Italian priest (1811-1860) who trained young priests in Turin and visited prisoners. He walked with condemned men to the gallows and is the patron of prison chaplains.

name: Saint Maximus of Turin
description: Bishop of Turin (d. c. 465) whose short, vivid sermons survive as a guide to pastoral preaching. He encouraged his people to seek Christ amid the turbulence of invasion.

name: Saint Josemaria Escriva
description: Spanish priest (1902-1975) who founded Opus Dei and taught that ordinary work and daily life are a path to holiness open to everyone.
patronOf: Lay Christians, workers, sanctification of work

name: The First Martyrs of the Church of Rome
description: Christians who died under Nero in 64 AD after the great fire of Rome. They were the first fruits of Rome's martyrs and their witness prepared the way for the faith's growth in the city.

name: Saint Junipero Serra
description: Spanish Franciscan (1713-1784) who founded missions across California. His legacy is debated, but he is remembered for pastoral dedication and tireless travel despite illness.

name: Saints Processus and Martinian
description: Two guards of Saint Peter in the Mamertine prison in Rome who were converted and baptised by him. They were martyred, and their relics rest in Saint Peter's Basilica.

name: Saint Anthony Zaccaria
description: Italian physician turned priest (1502-1539) who founded the Barnabites and encouraged frequent communion and devotion to Saint Paul. He urged his companions to 'be fools for Christ'.

name: Saint Willibald
description: English bishop (c. 700-787) who made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land and later served in Germany with Saint Boniface. He founded the monastery of Heidenheim and became bishop of Eichstatt.

name: Saints Priscilla and Aquila
description: A married couple, tentmakers, who hosted Saint Paul in Corinth and Ephesus and helped to instruct Apollos. They opened their home as a church and risked their lives for Paul.

name: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong and Companions
description: A group of 120 Chinese martyrs, from bishops to peasants, killed between the 1600s and 1900s. They included many ordinary lay men and women who kept the faith under persecution.

name: Saints Rufina and Secunda
description: Sisters who died as martyrs in Rome around 257 during Valerian's persecution. They are depicted with palms and jars of ointment and are honoured in the Lateran cathedral.

name: Saint Henry II
description: German emperor (973-1024) who devoted his reign to supporting the Church, founding the diocese of Bamberg and encouraging monastic reform. He and his wife, Saint Cunegund, lived in chaste marriage.

name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel
description: A feast honouring Mary as patroness of the Carmelite order, founded on Mount Carmel in the Holy Land. The brown scapular, worn in devotion, recalls her protection.
patronOf: Carmelites, those who wear the scapular

name: The Martyrs of Compiegne
description: Sixteen Carmelite nuns guillotined in Paris on July 17, 1794, during the French Revolution. They sang as they walked to the scaffold and offered their lives for peace.
patronOf: Religious sisters, peace in times of conflict

name: Saint Symphorosa and Her Seven Sons
description: A Roman widow martyred around 135 along with her seven sons for refusing to sacrifice to idols. Tradition holds that she encouraged each of her sons as they died.

name: Saint Macrina the Younger
description: Cappadocian nun (c. 330-379) who turned her family home into a community of prayer. She was teacher and guide to her brothers Basil and Gregory of Nyssa.

name: Saint Apollinaris of Ravenna
description: First bishop of Ravenna, tradition holds, a disciple of Saint Peter who evangelised the region and was martyred. The basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe honours him.

name: Saint Lawrence of Brindisi
description: Italian Capuchin (1559-1619) who spoke many languages and preached across Europe. He served as chaplain to imperial armies and was named a Doctor of the Church.

name: Saint Pantaleon
description: Physician of Nicomedia martyred around 305. His name means 'all-merciful', and he is one of the 'Holy Unmercenaries' who healed without charge.

name: Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus
description: The siblings of Bethany whose home welcomed Jesus. Martha served, Mary listened, and Lazarus was raised from the dead. Together they show friendship with Christ.
patronOf: Hosts, those who serve and those who pray

name: Saint Eusebius of Vercelli
description: Bishop of Vercelli (c. 283-371) who founded a community of clergy living in common and was exiled for defending the faith of Nicaea against Arian rulers.

name: Saint Nicodemus
description: A Pharisee who visited Jesus by night, defended him before the Sanhedrin and helped Joseph of Arimathea to bury his body. His quiet courage grew slowly into open faith.
patronOf: Those who seek God in secret

name: Dedication of the Basilica of Saint Mary Major
description: The oldest church in the West dedicated to Mary, built in Rome after the Council of Ephesus. The feast recalls a tradition of snow falling on the Esquiline Hill in summer.

name: The Transfiguration of the Lord
description: On a high mountain Jesus' face shone like the sun and Moses and Elijah appeared with him, while the voice of the Father said 'this is my beloved Son'. A glimpse of the glory to come.

name: Saint Cajetan
description: Italian priest (1480-1547) who co-founded the Theatines to renew the clergy and care for the sick. He believed in trusting providence completely, and cared for the poor and incurables.

name: Saint Jane Frances de Chantal
description: French noblewoman (1572-1641) who, after her husband's death, became friend of Saint Francis de Sales and co-founded the Visitation Sisters.
patronOf: Widows, parents, those who have lost a spouse

name: Saints Pontian and Hippolytus
description: A pope and a priest-theologian who quarrelled but reconciled when both were exiled to the mines of Sardinia. Both died there around 235, and their relics were returned to Rome.

name: Saint Stephen of Hungary
description: First king of Hungary (c. 975-1038) who led his people to Christianity, founded dioceses and monasteries, and cared for orphans and the poor.

name: Saint Hyacinth of Poland
description: Polish Dominican (c. 1185-1257) who carried the Gospel to Poland, Prussia and Kiev. He founded priories and is known as the 'Apostle of Poland'.

name: Saint Helena
description: Mother of Emperor Constantine (c. 250-330) who made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land in her old age. She built churches at Bethlehem and the Mount of Olives and honoured the places of Jesus' life.

name: Saint John Eudes
description: French priest (1601-1680) who preached parish missions, founded the Eudists to train priests and promoted devotion to the Hearts of Jesus and Mary.

name: Pope Saint Pius X
description: Pope from 1903 to 1914, born Giuseppe Sarto, who encouraged frequent Communion, young children's first Communion and the study of the catechism. He lived simply.

name: The Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
description: A feast celebrating Mary as queen of heaven, crowned in glory beside her Son. Her queenship is one of mercy and service, not of power.

name: Saint Louis IX of France
description: King of France (1214-1270) who built the Sainte-Chapelle, cared for the poor, judged under an oak tree and died on crusade. He is an example of a Christian ruler.
patronOf: Kings, the Third Order Franciscans, French monarchs

name: Saint Elizabeth Bichier des Ages
description: French religious (1773-1838) who, after the French Revolution, founded the Daughters of the Cross to teach children and care for the poor and sick.
patronOf: Teachers, those who help rebuild after upheaval

name: The Passion of Saint John the Baptist
description: The Church remembers the beheading of John the Baptist by Herod for speaking the truth about his marriage. His courage is a model for witness to truth.
patronOf: Those who speak the truth at cost

name: Saint Jeanne Jugan
description: French woman (1792-1879) who took an elderly blind woman into her home and began the Little Sisters of the Poor, who now care for the elderly in many countries.

name: Saint Aidan of Lindisfarne
description: Irish monk (d. 651) who founded the monastery of Lindisfarne and brought Christianity to Northumbria. He travelled on foot to meet people and gave away gifts to the poor.

name: Saint Giles
description: Hermit of the seventh or eighth century who lived in southern France and founded an abbey near Arles. Tradition holds he sheltered a wounded deer, and he is invoked as protector of the vulnerable.

name: The Martyrs of September
description: More than a hundred priests and religious killed in Paris in September 1792 for refusing to swear loyalty to the revolutionary state's church. They died praying and forgiving.

name: Saint Rose of Viterbo
description: Italian teenager (1233-1251) who preached in the streets of Viterbo, calling people to faith during a time of conflict. She was refused admission to a convent and lived in prayer at home.

name: Saint Bega
description: Seventh-century Irish princess who fled an arranged marriage and settled in Cumbria as a hermit. Tradition says she founded the nunnery at St Bees, which bears her name.

name: Saints Stephen Pongracz, Melchior Grodziecki and Mark Krizin
description: Three priests martyred in Kosice in 1619 for refusing to renounce their faith. They are remembered as witnesses to fidelity in the divided Europe of their day.
patronOf: Central Europe, those who stand firm in faith

name: The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
description: The Church celebrates the birthday of Mary, nine months after the feast of the Immaculate Conception. Her birth heralds the dawn of salvation, for Christ is born of her.

name: Saint Peter Claver
description: Spanish Jesuit (1580-1654) who ministered to enslaved Africans arriving in Cartagena, Colombia. He baptised some 300,000 people and called himself 'the slave of the slaves forever'.

name: Saint Nicholas of Tolentino
description: Italian Augustinian friar (c. 1245-1305) who preached, heard confessions and visited the sick. He is remembered for devotion to the souls in purgatory and the 'bread of Saint Nicholas'.
patronOf: Souls in purgatory, sailors, the sick

name: Saints Protus and Hyacinth
description: Two Roman brothers or servants martyred in the third century. Their tomb in the catacombs of Saint Hermes was found intact in the nineteenth century.

name: The Holy Name of Mary
description: A feast honouring the name of Mary, first celebrated in Spain and extended to the Church after the Christian victory at Vienna in 1683.
patronOf: Those who call on Mary's name

name: The Exaltation of the Holy Cross
description: The Church lifts up the cross as the sign of Christ's victory. The feast recalls the finding of the True Cross in Jerusalem and the triumph of love over death.

name: Our Lady of Sorrows
description: A feast recalling the sorrows of Mary, from Simeon's prophecy to her standing beneath the cross. Mary shares in her Son's suffering and comforts those who grieve.
patronOf: Those in grief, mothers who have lost children

name: Saint Joseph of Cupertino
description: Italian Franciscan (1603-1663) who struggled with learning but was marked by childlike faith and accounts of ecstasies. He is the patron of students and those who sit exams.

name: Saint Januarius
description: Bishop of Benevento martyred around 305 near Naples. A vial said to contain his blood is kept in Naples and, as tradition holds, liquefies on his feast.

name: Saints Andrew Kim Taegon, Paul Chong Hasang and Companions
description: 103 Korean martyrs killed between 1839 and 1867, among them the first Korean priest, Andrew Kim, and many laypeople. Korea's church began largely through lay believers.

name: Saint Maurice and Companions
description: Commander of the Theban Legion, said to have been martyred in Switzerland around 287 with his men for refusing to take part in pagan sacrifices.
patronOf: Soldiers, those who refuse unjust orders

name: Saint Sergius of Radonezh
description: Russian monk (c. 1314-1392) who founded the Trinity Lavra and became spiritual father of the Russian people. He blessed Prince Dmitri before the battle that began Russian freedom.
patronOf: Russia, monks, those who seek peace

name: Saints Cosmas and Damian
description: Twin brothers, physicians in Syria, who treated the sick without payment and were martyred around 287. They are honoured among the 'holy unmercenaries'.

name: Saint Wenceslaus of Bohemia
description: Duke of Bohemia (c. 907-935) who ruled with humility and generosity and was murdered by his brother. The Christmas carol 'Good King Wenceslas' honours his charity.
patronOf: Czech lands, rulers, those who give to the poor

name: The Holy Guardian Angels
description: A feast thanking God for the angels who watch over each person. Scripture and tradition teach that each of us is entrusted to the care of a guardian from birth until death.

name: Saint Dionysius the Areopagite
description: Athenian convert of Saint Paul on the Areopagus, according to the Acts of the Apostles, who became the first bishop of Athens. Tradition honours him as a martyr.

name: Our Lady of the Rosary
description: Pope Pius V established this feast in 1571 after the naval victory at Lepanto, attributed to the prayer of the Rosary. It invites the faithful to meditate on the life of Christ with Mary.

name: Saint Pelagia of Antioch
description: A fifteen-year-old girl of Antioch who, rather than be taken by soldiers, threw herself from a rooftop and died, according to tradition, in 311 or 312. She is honoured as a martyr of purity.

name: Saint Francis Borgia
description: Spanish duke (1510-1572) who became a Jesuit after the death of his wife. As third superior general, he strengthened the order's schools and missions.
patronOf: Those who change their lives, widowers

name: Saint John XXIII
description: Pope from 1958 to 1963 known as 'Good Pope John' who called the Second Vatican Council. He was admired for his warmth, humour and humility.

name: Saint Edward the Confessor
description: King of England (c. 1003-1066) known for piety and generosity. He rebuilt Westminster Abbey and was revered as the 'patron of kings' by English monarchs.

name: Pope Saint Callistus I
description: Pope from about 217 to 222, a former slave who became bishop of Rome. He extended mercy to repentant sinners and gave his name to the catacombs of Saint Callistus.

name: Saints John de Brebeuf, Isaac Jogues and Companions
description: Eight Jesuit missionaries and lay helpers martyred in the 1640s in North America. They lived among the Huron and other peoples and are patrons of Canada.

name: Saint Paul of the Cross
description: Italian mystic (1694-1775) who founded the Passionists to preach the love of Christ shown in his Passion. He directed souls in the deepest prayer and loved the poor.

name: Saint Hilarion
description: Palestinian hermit (c. 291-371) who lived in the desert near Gaza and brought monasticism to Palestine. Many came to him seeking guidance and healing.

name: Saint John of Capistrano
description: Italian Franciscan (1386-1456) who preached across Europe, reformed the order and helped organise the defence of Belgrade in 1456 against the Ottoman advance.

name: Saint Anthony Mary Claret
description: Spanish priest and missionary bishop (1807-1870) who founded the Claretians and served in Cuba. He preached in the open air and used the press to spread the Gospel.

name: The Forty Martyrs of England and Wales
description: Forty Catholics, priests and laypeople, executed between 1535 and 1679 for their faith. They died on the scaffold, often forgiving those who condemned them.

name: Alfred the Great
description: King of Wessex (849-899) who defended Christian England against Viking invaders, promoted learning and translated books into English. He was a wise and merciful ruler.

name: Saint Frumentius
description: Syrian-born missionary (d. c. 380) captured as a boy and brought to Axum, who later became the first bishop of Ethiopia, ordained by Saint Athanasius.

name: Saint Narcissus of Jerusalem
description: Bishop of Jerusalem (c. 99-215) who, tradition says, changed water to oil for the lamps on Easter vigil. After false accusations he retired as a hermit and later returned.

name: Saint Alphonsus Rodriguez
description: Spanish Jesuit lay brother (1533-1617) who after the death of his wife and children became porter of a college in Majorca. He gave guidance to students, including Saint Peter Claver.

name: Saint Wolfgang of Regensburg
description: German bishop (c. 924-994) who reformed monasteries, cared for the poor and educated the future emperor Henry II. He later lived as a hermit in Austria.

name: All Saints
description: The Church honours all those who have lived and died in Christ and now rejoice in heaven, known and unknown. It is a feast of hope for all who follow the way of holiness.
patronOf: All the saints, all of the faithful

name: The Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed
description: All Souls' Day is a day of prayer for those who have died. The Church remembers family, friends and strangers and entrusts them to the mercy of God.

name: Saint Charles Borromeo
description: Archbishop of Milan (1538-1584) who implemented the reforms of the Council of Trent, founded seminaries and ministered to the plague-stricken of Milan.

name: Saints Zechariah and Elizabeth
description: The parents of John the Baptist, described in Luke's Gospel as righteous before God. Elizabeth welcomed Mary at the Visitation, and Zechariah proclaimed the Benedictus.
patronOf: Parents, those who wait for answered prayer

name: Saint Leonard of Noblac
description: Frankish hermit of the sixth century, said to have been freed from prison through the prayer of Saint Remigius. He is invoked by prisoners and captives.

name: Saint Willibrord
description: Northumbrian monk (658-739) who became the first bishop of Utrecht and apostle of the Frisians. He founded the abbey of Echternach in Luxembourg.

name: Blessed John Duns Scotus
description: Scottish Franciscan philosopher and theologian (c. 1266-1308), the 'Subtle Doctor', who defended the Immaculate Conception and taught that Christ's incarnation springs from love.

name: Pope Saint Leo the Great
description: Pope from 440 to 461 whose letter to Flavian shaped the Council of Chalcedon's teaching on Christ. He met Attila and persuaded him to spare Rome.
patronOf: Popes, those who seek peace, theologians

name: Saint Martin of Tours
description: Roman soldier (c. 316-397) who cut his cloak in two to share with a beggar and later became bishop of Tours. His generosity made him one of the best-loved saints of Europe.
patronOf: Soldiers, the poor, those who give

name: Saint Josaphat
description: Ukrainian Basilian monk and archbishop of Polotsk (c. 1580-1623) who worked for unity between Eastern and Western Christians. He was martyred and is honoured in the Eastern Catholic Churches.

name: Saint Margaret of Scotland
description: Anglo-Saxon princess (c. 1045-1093) who became queen of Scotland. She cared for orphans and the poor, reformed church life and was a devoted mother of eight.

name: Dedication of the Basilicas of Saints Peter and Paul
description: The feast marks the dedication of the great basilicas in Rome built over the tombs of the two apostles. It reminds us of the Church's roots in apostolic witness.

name: Saint Mechtilde of Helfta
description: German Benedictine nun and mystic (1240-1298) at the monastery of Helfta. Her visions of the Sacred Heart and her prayers were widely read in the Middle Ages.

name: Saint Edmund the Martyr
description: King of East Anglia (c. 841-869) killed by Danish invaders after refusing to renounce Christ. He became one of England's most honoured martyr-kings.
patronOf: Kings, East Anglia, those facing persecution

name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
description: A feast marking the dedication of Mary to God in the Temple as a child. It recalls her complete offering of herself, long before the Annunciation.

name: Saint Andrew Dung-Lac and Companions
description: 117 Vietnamese martyrs killed between 1625 and 1886, including priests, catechists and laypeople. Their witness is the foundation of the Church in Vietnam.

name: Saint Leonard of Port Maurice
description: Italian Franciscan (1676-1751) who preached parish missions throughout Italy and promoted the Stations of the Cross. He is the patron of parish missions.
patronOf: Parish missionaries, the Stations of the Cross

name: Saint Virgil of Salzburg
description: Irish monk (c. 700-784) who became bishop of Salzburg and encouraged scholarship. He championed a mission to the Slavs and completed the cathedral of Salzburg.

name: Saint Catherine Laboure
description: French Daughter of Charity (1806-1876) who in 1830 saw Mary and received the design of the Miraculous Medal. She served quietly for decades as a nurse of the elderly.
patronOf: The Miraculous Medal, the elderly, nurses

name: Saint Saturninus of Toulouse
description: First bishop of Toulouse, martyred around 257 after refusing to sacrifice. According to tradition he was tied to a bull and dragged through the streets of the city.

name: Blessed Charles de Foucauld
description: French soldier turned hermit (1858-1916) who lived among the Tuareg in the Sahara, serving through quiet friendship and prayer. His spiritual vision inspired the Little Brothers of Jesus.
patronOf: Hermits, those who live among strangers

name: Saint Raphael Kalinowski
description: Polish engineer and soldier (1835-1907) who endured exile in Siberia before becoming a Carmelite. He restored the Discalced Carmelites in Poland and promoted Christian unity.

name: Saint Sabbas the Sanctified
description: Palestinian abbot (439-532) who founded the monastery of Mar Saba in the Judean desert, which has continued to this day. He guided thousands of monks and defended Chalcedon.
patronOf: Monks, those who live in the desert

name: The Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary
description: The Church celebrates the belief that Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her existence, in view of the merits of her Son.

name: Our Lady of Loreto
description: A feast recalling the tradition of the Holy House of Nazareth, said to have been carried to Loreto, Italy. It honours the Holy Family's home and the mystery of the Incarnation.
patronOf: Pilots, those who travel by air

name: Pope Saint Damasus I
description: Pope from 366 to 384 who commissioned Saint Jerome to prepare a Latin translation of the Bible. He restored the catacombs and honoured the martyrs with verses.

name: Saint Virginia Centurione Bracelli
description: Genoese widow (1587-1651) who gave her life to the poor and abandoned, opening a hospice and organizing aid for those in need. She was canonized in 2003.

name: Saint Adelaide of Burgundy
description: Empress (931-999) who endured imprisonment and exile and later reigned as co-regent. She used her power to found monasteries and care for the poor.

name: Saint Olympias
description: Constantinopolitan widow and deaconess (c. 361-408) who gave away her wealth to the Church and the poor. She stood loyally with Saint John Chrysostom during his exile.

name: Saint Gatian of Tours
description: Traditional first bishop of Tours (third century) who evangelised Gaul and ministered in secret during persecution, celebrating Mass in caves.

name: Blessed Urban V
description: Pope from 1362 to 1370 who tried to restore the papacy to Rome from Avignon. He supported education, founded colleges and lived a simple life.

name: Saint Dominic of Silos
description: Spanish Benedictine abbot (c. 1000-1073) who renewed the monastery of Silos and ransomed captives from the Moors. He is invoked by expectant mothers.

name: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
description: Italian-born sister (1850-1917) who founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart and served Italian immigrants in the United States, building hospitals, schools and orphanages.

name: Saint John of Kanty
description: Polish priest and professor (1390-1473) at Krakow known for generosity to the poor and for his humility. He taught with gentleness and lived frugally.

name: Saints Adam and Eve
description: The Church remembers the first parents on the eve of Christmas, as Christ comes to restore what was lost. Their story is the beginning of the promise of salvation.
patronOf: Families, those who hope for redemption

name: The Nativity of the Lord
description: On Christmas the Church celebrates the birth of Jesus in Bethlehem. God becomes a child, laid in a manger, as the sign of his closeness to every person.

name: The Holy Innocents
description: The children of Bethlehem killed by King Herod in his attempt to destroy the infant Jesus. The Church honours them as the first martyrs, who gave witness not by words but by their deaths.

name: Saint Thomas Becket
description: Archbishop of Canterbury (c. 1118-1170) who defended the freedom of the Church against King Henry II and was murdered in his cathedral. His shrine drew pilgrims for centuries.
patronOf: Secular clergy, those who stand for conscience

name: Saint Sabinus of Spoleto
description: Bishop of Assisi martyred around 303 under Diocletian. He is honoured in central Italy for his steadfast faith and for the healing of a blind man.

name: Pope Saint Sylvester I
description: Pope from 314 to 335 during the reign of Constantine. The Church grew in peace and the first Roman basilicas were built. The year ends on his feast day.
patronOf: The end of the year, thanksgiving
